title: Procedures
summary: Bedside ICU procedures: ultrasound-guided central venous and arterial cannulation, thoracentesis and chest drains, lumbar puncture, paracentesis and pericardiocentesis, with coagulation thresholds, local anaesthetic safety and Indian context.

topics.title: Central venous catheter insertion
topics.summary: Site choice, real-time ultrasound, confirming venous placement before dilation, tip position and complications.

definition.text: CVC indications: vasopressors or irritant infusions, poor peripheral access, CVP/ScvO₂ monitoring, RRT or plasmapheresis (dialysis catheter), transvenous pacing. ASA 2020 recommends real-time ultrasound for internal jugular access and confirmation of venous placement before dilation.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.detail: Consent where possible; check coagulation and platelets (correction rarely needed for compressible sites); time-out; full sterile barrier and alcoholic chlorhexidine.

steps.title: Choose site
steps.detail: IJ with ultrasound: lowest mechanical risk and easy compression; subclavian: lowest infection and thrombosis risk but pneumothorax risk; femoral: fast in arrest/coagulopathy but highest infection and thrombosis risk.

steps.title: Ultrasound
steps.detail: Pre-scan vessel patency and size; real-time needle guidance (short- or long-axis) with the needle tip visualised.

steps.title: Position
steps.detail: Head-down (Trendelenburg) for IJ/subclavian to distend veins and reduce air embolism risk.

steps.title: Confirm venous placement before dilating
steps.detail: Ultrasound view of the wire in the vein (long axis), manometry or pressure waveform transduction; never dilate an uncertain vessel.

steps.title: Keep control of the wire
steps.detail: Never let go of the guidewire; check the wire is complete after removal.

steps.title: Confirm tip and exclude pneumothorax
steps.detail: Tip at the lower SVC / cavo-atrial junction; chest X-ray, or ultrasound with agitated saline (bubbles in RA within 2 s) and lung sliding check.

steps.title: Arterial cannulation with dilator or catheter
steps.detail: Leave the device in place, do not remove; call vascular surgery / interventional radiology.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: max ~300 mg plain = 30 mL of 1% (10 mg/mL) or 15 mL of 2%.

tables.title: CVC site comparison
rows: Ultrasound-friendly; compressible; straight path to SVC (right)
Carotid puncture; patient comfort; tracheostomy contamination
Pneumothorax; non-compressible artery; harder with ultrasound
Fast, away from airway and CPR

tables.title: Bleeding risk and coagulation for bedside procedures (SIR 2019)
tables.caption: Consensus thresholds; emergencies proceed with the most experienced operator and ultrasound.

redFlags.text: New hypotension, hypoxaemia or neurological deficit during or after insertion: consider pneumothorax, haemothorax, air embolism (left lateral head-down, 100% oxygen) or arterial injury.
Perioral tingling, seizures or arrhythmia after local anaesthetic: stop injecting, call for help, manage airway and give 20% lipid emulsion (1.5 mL/kg bolus) for LAST.

pitfalls.text: Dilating before confirming the wire is in the vein.
Routine FFP or platelets before ultrasound-guided CVC in mild coagulopathy.

pearls.text: PACER: with platelets 10-50 × 10⁹/L, omitting a prophylactic platelet unit before CVC placement increased catheter-related bleeding (11.9% vs 4.8%).

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Mechanical complications (arterial puncture, pneumothorax, malposition) occur at insertion and are reduced by ultrasound; infectious and thrombotic complications accumulate with catheter days and are site- and maintenance-dependent.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ASA 2020 practice guidelines [ASA 2020].
- International recommendations on ultrasound-guided vascular access [Lamperti 2012]; ESAIC 2020 [Lamperti 2020].
- PACER trial [van Baarle 2023]; SIR 2019 periprocedural thresholds [Patel 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Subclavian versus IJ as the default site; ultrasound-guided subclavian/axillary approaches; prophylactic platelets in severe thrombocytopenia.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Ultrasound machines are now widely available in Indian tertiary ICUs; in district hospitals landmark technique is still used - train with simulation and prefer femoral or IJ with ultrasound when possible.
- Triple-lumen 7 Fr CVCs and 12-13.5 Fr dialysis catheters are standard stock; antimicrobial-impregnated catheters are costlier and rarely used.

quiz.stem: Before dilating during CVC insertion, you should:
options: Confirm the wire is in the vein

quiz.stem: Dilator found in the carotid artery:
options: Leave in place; call vascular surgery

topics.title: Arterial line insertion and troubleshooting
topics.summary: Radial cannulation with ultrasound, transducer set-up, zeroing, and the square-wave test.

definition.text: Arterial cannulation provides continuous blood pressure and frequent blood gas sampling. Indications: vasopressors, haemodynamic instability, frequent ABGs, unreliable NIBP. Radial is first choice; femoral and brachial are alternatives.

steps.title: Site
steps.detail: Radial (first choice) > femoral > brachial (end artery, use with caution) > dorsalis pedis.

steps.title: Ultrasound
steps.detail: Ultrasound guidance increases first-pass success and reduces haematoma.

steps.title: Technique
steps.detail: Wrist extended; aseptic; 20 G catheter (radial) via direct puncture or Seldinger; secure and dress.

steps.title: Transducer
steps.detail: Pressure bag at 300 mmHg giving ~3 mL/h flush of saline; no glucose-containing flush.

steps.title: Zero and level
steps.detail: Level the transducer at the phlebostatic axis (4th intercostal space, mid-axillary line); zero to atmosphere; re-level after bed changes.

steps.title: Check damping
steps.detail: Fast-flush (square-wave) test: 1-2 oscillations = optimal; none = overdamped (air, clot, kink); many = underdamped (stiff long tubing).

steps.title: Remove
steps.detail: Remove when no longer needed; check hand perfusion daily.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: max ~300 mg plain = 30 mL of 1% (10 mg/mL) or 15 mL of 2%.

tables.title: Arterial waveform troubleshooting
rows: Falsely low systolic, high diastolic; MAP roughly preserved
Remove air bubbles, clot, kinks; check bag pressure
Overshoot: falsely high systolic, low diastolic

redFlags.text: Pale, cold or painful hand after radial cannulation: remove the catheter and assess perfusion.
Accidental drug injection into an arterial line: stop, leave catheter, seek vascular advice.

pitfalls.text: Trusting a systolic value from an overdamped trace - use MAP for decisions.

pearls.text: The modified Allen test predicts ischaemia poorly; ultrasound of ulnar flow and clinical monitoring are more useful.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Catheter-tubing-transducer systems are second-order systems with a natural frequency and damping coefficient; distortion causes systematic errors in systolic and diastolic values while MAP is least affected.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- Ultrasound-guided arterial access improves success [Lamperti 2020; Lamperti 2012].
- Practical guidance [IBCC].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Infection risk of arterial lines relative to CVCs (similar per catheter-day in some studies).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Disposable transducer kits add cost; some units reuse domes - follow manufacturer and infection-control policy.

topics.title: Thoracentesis and chest drain insertion
topics.summary: Ultrasound-guided pleural aspiration, interpreting pleural fluid, intercostal drain insertion and drain management.

definition.text: BTS 2023: use thoracic ultrasound for all pleural procedures for fluid; insert drains in the 'triangle of safety'; small-bore Seldinger drains are suitable for most effusions, pneumothorax and pleural infection.

steps.title: Image
steps.detail: Ultrasound to mark or guide the site; note depth, diaphragm and organs; ICU patients often supine - lateral approach in mid- to posterior axillary line.

steps.title: Site
steps.detail: Triangle of safety: anterior border of latissimus dorsi, lateral border of pectoralis major, line at the 5th intercostal space (nipple level); insert just above the rib.

steps.title: Diagnostic tap
steps.detail: Send protein, LDH, pH (blood gas syringe), glucose, cell count, Gram stain and culture (blood-culture bottles), cytology, and ADA where TB is suspected.

steps.title: Therapeutic tap
steps.detail: Stop if chest tightness, cough or vasovagal symptoms; limit volume at one sitting (commonly 1-1.5 L) to avoid re-expansion oedema.

steps.title: Chest drain
steps.detail: Seldinger 12-14 Fr for most indications; larger bore for haemothorax or large air leaks; secure, connect to underwater seal.

steps.title: Pleural infection
steps.detail: Drain if frank pus, pH < 7.2 or positive Gram stain/culture; antibiotics; consider intrapleural tPA + DNase if poor drainage; surgical referral if failing.

steps.title: Drain care
steps.detail: Never clamp a bubbling drain; daily CXR/US and output; remove when lung re-expanded and air leak stops or fluid < ~200 mL/day (local protocol).

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: max ~300 mg plain = 30 mL of 1% (10 mg/mL) or 15 mL of 2%.

doseCards.dose: Alteplase 10 mg + dornase 5 mg twice daily for 3 days

tables.title: Light's criteria (exudate if any one present)
rows: > 2/3 upper limit of normal serum LDH

redFlags.text: Sudden hypoxaemia and frothy sputum after draining a large effusion: re-expansion pulmonary oedema.
Tension pneumothorax in a ventilated patient (hypotension, rising airway pressures, absent lung sliding): needle or finger decompression then drain.

pitfalls.text: Inserting a drain without ultrasound for a fluid collection.
Clamping a drain that is bubbling.

pearls.text: Light's criteria misclassify about 25% of transudates in patients on diuretics as exudates - check serum-pleural albumin gradient (> 12 g/L favours transudate).

nodes.text: US-guided diagnostic aspiration: pH, protein, LDH, glucose, culture
Pus, pH < 7.2 or positive Gram stain?
Intrapleural tPA + DNase or surgical referral
Large effusion impairing oxygenation or weaning?

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Effusions in ICU are mostly transudates (heart failure, fluid overload, hypoalbuminaemia, atelectasis) but parapneumonic effusions and haemothorax need drainage. Removing large effusions improves oxygenation modestly and may aid weaning.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- BTS 2023 pleural guideline [Roberts 2023].
- MIST2: tPA + DNase improved radiographic drainage and reduced surgical referral [Rahman 2011].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Volume limits for therapeutic thoracentesis (pleural manometry); drainage of transudates in ventilated patients.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Tuberculous effusion is common: pleural ADA (> 40 units/L supportive) with lymphocytic exudate; avoid drains for uncomplicated TB effusions.
- Empyema from delayed presentation is frequent; dornase alfa is expensive - urokinase or streptokinase are sometimes used locally (weaker evidence).

quiz.stem: Indication for chest drain in parapneumonic effusion:
Never do this with a bubbling drain:

options: tPA 10 mg + DNase 5 mg BD for 3 days

topics.title: Lumbar puncture in the ICU
topics.summary: When to scan first, anticoagulant timing, technique, opening pressure and CSF tests.

definition.text: LP is needed for suspected meningitis/encephalitis, subarachnoid haemorrhage with negative CT, Guillain-Barré syndrome and some neurological disorders. Never delay antibiotics for imaging or LP in suspected bacterial meningitis.

steps.title: Antibiotics first
steps.detail: If bacterial meningitis is suspected and LP will be delayed, take blood cultures and give antibiotics (and dexamethasone) immediately.

steps.title: CT before LP if
steps.detail: Focal neurological deficit, new-onset seizures, GCS < 10, severe immunocompromise (ESCMID).

steps.title: Coagulation and anticoagulants
steps.detail: Prophylactic LMWH: wait 12 h; therapeutic LMWH: 24 h; SC UFH 5,000 units: 4-6 h; apixaban/rivaroxaban: 72 h; clopidogrel: 5-7 days; warfarin: normal INR. Platelets commonly ≥ 50 × 10⁹/L.

steps.title: Position and technique
steps.detail: Lateral decubitus (for accurate opening pressure) at L3/4 or L4/5; atraumatic (pencil-point) needle reduces post-dural puncture headache.

steps.title: Opening pressure
steps.detail: Measure with a manometer in lateral position, legs extended; normal about 10-20 cmH₂O; > 25 cmH₂O is raised (consider cryptococcal meningitis, IIH, venous sinus thrombosis).

steps.title: Samples
steps.detail: Cell count (tubes 1 and 4 for SAH), protein, glucose with paired plasma glucose, Gram stain and culture, PCR (HSV, enterovirus), cryptococcal antigen, AFB/GeneXpert, xanthochromia (> 12 h after SAH onset).

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: max ~300 mg plain = 30 mL of 1% (10 mg/mL) or 15 mL of 2%.

redFlags.text: Deterioration after LP (falling GCS, new pupil asymmetry) - suspect herniation; treat raised ICP and image urgently.

pitfalls.text: Delaying antibiotics for CT and LP.
Doing LP on therapeutic LMWH or a DOAC without checking timing.

pearls.text: CSF:blood glucose ratio < 0.4 is more useful than an absolute CSF glucose in hyperglycaemic patients.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: LP risks are herniation in patients with mass effect or obstructive hydrocephalus, spinal haematoma in coagulopathy, infection and post-dural puncture headache from CSF leak.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ESCMID 2016 meningitis guideline [van de Beek 2016].
- ASRA 2018 neuraxial anticoagulation timing, used by analogy for LP [Horlocker 2018].
- Atraumatic needles reduce PDPH [Nath 2018].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Safe platelet threshold for LP (often 40-50 × 10⁹/L; lower in haematology practice).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- TB meningitis, cryptococcal meningitis and scrub typhus/JE encephalitis are key differentials in India - send CSF ADA, GeneXpert and cryptococcal antigen where suspected.
- Manometers are often missing from LP sets; request them so that opening pressure is recorded.

topics.title: Paracentesis (diagnostic and large-volume)
topics.summary: Site, safety in coagulopathy, essential tests, SAAG, SBP diagnosis and albumin after large-volume paracentesis.

definition.text: Diagnostic paracentesis for every patient with cirrhosis and ascites admitted to hospital or deteriorating (SBP screening). Large-volume paracentesis (LVP) for tense or refractory ascites. Routine FFP or platelets are not recommended before paracentesis.

steps.title: Indication
steps.detail: New ascites, any hospital admission with ascites, fever, encephalopathy, AKI or GI bleed in cirrhosis.

steps.title: Site
steps.detail: Left lower quadrant, about 2 finger-breadths medial and cephalad to the anterior superior iliac spine; ultrasound guidance; avoid inferior epigastric vessels and scars.

steps.title: Coagulopathy
steps.detail: Do not routinely give FFP or platelets; avoid in DIC or clinically evident fibrinolysis.

steps.title: Tests
steps.detail: Cell count and differential, albumin (SAAG), total protein, culture in blood culture bottles at the bedside (10 mL each); amylase, cytology, ADA as indicated.

steps.title: Interpret
steps.detail: SBP: neutrophils ≥ 250/µL. SAAG ≥ 1.1 g/dL = portal hypertension; total protein < 1.5 g/dL = higher SBP risk.

steps.title: LVP
steps.detail: Remove ascites to dryness if tolerated; give 20% albumin 6-8 g/L removed when > 5 L.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: max ~300 mg plain = 30 mL of 1% (10 mg/mL) or 15 mL of 2%.
8 L removed: 48-64 g albumin = 240-320 mL of 20% albumin (about 2.5-3 bottles of 100 mL).

redFlags.text: Abdominal pain, falling haemoglobin or hypotension after paracentesis: suspect abdominal wall haematoma or haemoperitoneum (inferior epigastric injury).

pitfalls.text: Delaying diagnostic paracentesis for INR correction.
Sending ascitic fluid in a sterile container only - culture yield is higher when inoculated into blood culture bottles at the bedside.

pearls.text: Polymicrobial growth with very high protein or low glucose suggests secondary (surgical) peritonitis - image for perforation.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: LVP without albumin can cause post-paracentesis circulatory dysfunction (activation of renin-angiotensin, AKI, hyponatraemia); albumin expands effective arterial volume.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- AASLD 2021 practice guidance [Biggins 2021].
- SIR 2019 classifies paracentesis as low bleeding risk [Patel 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Albumin for LVP < 5 L in patients with AKI or ACLF.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Albumin is costly; prioritise LVP > 5 L and SBP/HRS indications. Tuberculous peritonitis is a common cause of high-protein, low-SAAG, lymphocytic ascites (ADA helpful).

options: Give vitamin K and wait 24 h

topics.title: Pericardiocentesis
topics.summary: Echo-guided pericardial drainage for tamponade: approach, confirmation, drain management and when to go to surgery.

definition.text: Pericardiocentesis is indicated for cardiac tamponade and for large or suspected purulent/neoplastic effusions. Echo guidance is recommended. Aortic dissection and traumatic haemopericardium are relative contraindications: surgical drainage is preferred.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.detail: Echo: effusion with RA/RV diastolic collapse, plethoric IVC, respiratory variation of mitral inflow; clinical hypotension and tachycardia.

steps.title: Resuscitate
steps.detail: Fluid bolus may transiently help; avoid positive-pressure ventilation and sedation if possible (may precipitate arrest).

steps.title: Approach
steps.detail: Echo-guided at the site with the largest fluid collection closest to the skin (apical, parasternal or subxiphoid); subxiphoid aims at the left shoulder at 30-45°.

steps.title: Confirm needle position
steps.detail: Echo with agitated saline in the pericardial space; then pass wire and pigtail catheter (Seldinger).

steps.title: Drain
steps.detail: Drain in steps (about < 1 L at once) to reduce pericardial decompression syndrome; leave the pigtail; remove when output < 25-30 mL/day.

steps.title: Send fluid
steps.detail: Cell count, protein, LDH, glucose, Gram stain, culture, AFB/GeneXpert, ADA, cytology.

steps.title: Surgical drainage
steps.detail: Aortic dissection, trauma, purulent loculated effusion, recurrent or clotted haemopericardium after cardiac surgery.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: max ~300 mg plain = 30 mL of 1% (10 mg/mL) or 15 mL of 2%.

redFlags.text: Tamponade with type A aortic dissection: urgent surgery; pericardiocentesis only to prevent imminent death, removing small volumes.

pitfalls.text: Intubating a patient with tamponade before drainage - induction and positive pressure can cause collapse.
Draining a large chronic effusion completely at once.

pearls.text: Pericardial ADA > 40 units/L supports tuberculous pericarditis - common in India.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Tamponade occurs when intrapericardial pressure exceeds cardiac filling pressures; the rate of accumulation matters more than volume (200 mL acutely vs > 1 L chronically). Ventricular interdependence produces pulsus paradoxus.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ESC 2015 pericardial guideline (procedural detail) [Adler 2015].
- ESC 2025 myocarditis and pericarditis guideline update [Schulz-Menger 2025].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Extended drainage to reduce recurrence; timing of drain removal.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Tuberculous pericarditis is a leading cause of large effusions in India; send ADA, GeneXpert and consider anti-tubercular therapy.
- Pigtail pericardial kits may not be available outside cath labs - a CVC set over a wire is a common improvisation (smaller lumen, blocks more easily).

options: Drain in steps (< 1 L at once)

drugs.name: Lidocaine (lignocaine)
drugs.adultDose: Infiltration with 1% (10 mg/mL) or 2% solution. Maximum: 4.5 mg/kg plain (about 300 mg), 7 mg/kg with adrenaline (about 500 mg).
drugs.cautions: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (perioral tingling, tinnitus, seizures, arrhythmia, arrest); aspirate before injecting; avoid adrenaline-containing solutions at end-arterial sites.
drugs.monitoring: Neurological symptoms and ECG during and after large-volume infiltration.
drugs.verify: Maximum dose limits vary by source (some cite 3 mg/kg plain); use the local procedural policy.

drugs.name: Lipid emulsion 20%
drugs.class: Antidote for local anaesthetic systemic toxicity
drugs.indications: LAST with seizures, arrhythmia or cardiovascular collapse
drugs.adultDose: > 70 kg: 100 mL bolus over 2-3 min, then 200-250 mL over 15-20 min. ≤ 70 kg: 1.5 mL/kg bolus over 2-3 min, then 0.25 mL/kg/min. Repeat bolus once or twice and double infusion rate if unstable; maximum about 12 mL/kg.
drugs.preparationIndia: 20% lipid emulsion bags (parenteral nutrition products, e.g. 100 mL and 250 mL).
drugs.cautions: Pancreatitis and lipaemic interference with labs; use with standard ACLS (reduced adrenaline doses ≤ 1 mcg/kg).

drugs.name: Intrapleural alteplase + dornase alfa
drugs.indications: Pleural infection with poor drainage despite a chest drain
drugs.adultDose: Alteplase 10 mg + dornase alfa 5 mg intrapleurally twice daily for 3 days (6 doses), each clamped for 1 h.
drugs.cautions: Pleural bleeding; check coagulation and platelets; avoid with bronchopleural fistula.
drugs.verify: Dornase alfa availability and cost in India; local protocol for dilution (commonly in 30 mL saline).

drugs.name: Human albumin 20%
drugs.adultDose: 6-8 g albumin per litre of ascites removed (e.g. 8 L removed: 48-64 g).
drugs.preparationIndia: 20% (20 g in 100 mL) and 5% vials; costly in India.

BTS advises stopping with symptoms; numeric limits are practice-based.
